# Keplor V3 — Copilot project rules

Read `START_HERE.md`, `KEPLOR_V3_MASTER_SPEC.md`, and the relevant documents in `docs/` before making changes.

## Non-negotiable
- The canonical brand direction is premium, restrained, editorial, near-black and violet. Do not convert the site into a cream/orange, generic SaaS, bento-grid, or template aesthetic.
- Core colors: ink `#050507`, Keplor purple `#36006D`. Supporting violet/indigo/blue/cyan are restrained lighting accents, not competing brand colors.
- Preserve negative space, large editorial typography, thin dividers, open service rows, and deliberate hierarchy.
- The hero's signature visual is a violet pixel Predictive Arc. Do not replace it with a sphere, planet, particle globe, stock image, or unrelated 3D object.
- Never invent testimonials, customer logos, usage metrics, uptime figures, certifications, team biographies, jobs, office addresses, public email addresses, pricing, or product/API claims.
- No fake form submission. If no backend is configured, explain the form is a prototype and provide copy-to-clipboard/email-client fallback only where genuinely implemented.
- Keep Next.js 14 App Router, React 18, TypeScript, Tailwind, and static export. Do not upgrade major versions or add dependencies without documenting the reason.
- No deployment, push, merge, DNS, or hosting changes unless explicitly requested.
- Do not mark tasks complete without running relevant checks and inspecting actual browser output/screenshots when available.
- Prefer accessible semantic HTML, keyboard-visible focus, reduced-motion support, responsive layouts, and efficient animation.
- Keep edits focused. Before large changes, inspect git diff and existing files. Never use destructive resets or overwrite user work without explicit permission.
